title: Geocaching for Families: A Free Real-Life Treasure Hunt
description: Geocaching explained for families: how the free app works, what you find in a cache, the swap rules, and tips for little treasure hunters and teens.
h1: Geocaching: a free real-life treasure hunt
intro: There are hidden containers all around you, in parks, woods and even towns, waiting to be found. Geocaching turns any walk into a treasure hunt.

image.alt: A boy and girl walking across a green field

cardText: How geocaching works and tips for little hunters and teens.

blocks.title: Scout’s geocaching tip
blocks.text: Start with “easy” caches near paths. If you trade a trinket, leave something of equal or greater value, and always sign the log.
points: Be discreet so non-geocachers don’t find the cache
Put it back exactly where you found it

sections.html: Geocachers hide containers (“caches”) and post their GPS locations online. You use the official app or website to navigate to them, find the cache, sign the logbook and log your find. A free basic membership gives access to lots of caches.
Usually a logbook and sometimes small trinkets to swap. Some caches hold “trackables” that travel from cache to cache around the world.
Harder puzzle caches and multi-stage hunts are proper brain-teasers. It’s a gateway to escape rooms and longer nature adventures.

faqs.a: Yes. A free basic account with the official geocaching app gives access to many caches. A paid membership unlocks more.
